sources.label: Wikipedia, "Alpha Apodis"
sources.quote: Alpha Apodis, also named Paradys, is the brightest star in the southern circumpolar constellation of Apus.

introduction.text: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 869 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,202 K, so 55.698 solar radii.

sources.label: McDonald et al. (2017), Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society 471 770-791

sources.label: Wikipedia, "Alpha Apodis"
sources.quote: It had the Greek alpha designation as part of the constellation which Johann Bayer called Apis Indica in his 1603 Uranometria star atlas.
